summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, diabetes, and prior stroke was admitted for acute worsening of shortness of breath and leg swelling. The exacerbation was due to accidentally missing five days of Lasix after mistakenly refilling metoprolol instead. He received IV diuresis with significant fluid removal and improvement in symptoms. His INR was supratherapeutic (peaking at 3.9), so warfarin was held. He was transitioned from Lasix to torsemide 40mg daily, and discharge instructions emphasized daily weight monitoring and outpatient INR follow-up. He was discharged stable, with improved edema and respiratory status.
